intro: On the shore of Lake Beyşehir, a sultan once built a town for himself. You are at Kubadabad Palace, in Konya province, raised by Alâeddin Keykubad I in 1226–1237. The figured tiles that once lined its walls now hang in the Karatay Museum in Konya.
history: Alâeddin Keykubad I had a palace town built for himself on the western shore of Lake Beyşehir. Picture it: a great palace and a lesser one, a boatyard, hunting lodges, and a pavilion on an island in the lake. The figured tiles uncovered in excavations from 1949 onwards are the richest source we have for how a Seljuk palace was decorated.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Great Palace and the Lesser Palace. Look for the remains of the boatyard, and then turn your eyes to the island pavilion.
facts: Did you know? The tiles show the sultan himself, along with hunting birds, sirens and double-headed eagles. They are evidence that the prohibition on figures did not hold inside a Seljuk palace. The figured tiles that lined the palace walls are displayed today in the Karatay Museum in Konya.
outro: This brings our tour of Kubadabad Palace to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let this lakeside palace keep its quiet for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
